context_requirements: Expression of histamine receptors (HRH1/HRH2/HRH3/HRH4) on the cancer cell
Histamine-dependent autocrine/paracrine survival or proliferative signaling
Intact apoptotic machinery, particularly wild-type TP53 for the strongest response
Sufficient intracellular concentration of the antagonist (some effects are off-target and concentration-dependent)
falsifiers: No consistent transcriptional response across any of the nine cell lines at 6 h or 24 h
Absence of proliferation_down or apoptosis signatures at 24 h in MCF7 despite reported TP53-dependent apoptosis
Lack of any dose-dependent or time-dependent changes in histamine-receptor-expressing lines
Predominant upregulation of proliferation genes rather than downregulation

evidence.supports: H1 antagonist diphenhydramine induces apoptosis in T-ALL lines, suggesting H1 antagonism can trigger cell death
Desloratadine induces TP53-dependent apoptosis in MCF-7 breast cancer cells with upregulation of TP53, FAS, BAX
Ebastine, an H1 antagonist, exerts antitumor activity via AMPK/ULK1-dependent autophagy and apoptosis in osteosarcoma
Loratadine, an H1 antagonist, inhibits histamine-induced fibroblast proliferation and modulates apoptosis markers
Histamine receptor expression varies across hematological cancer lines and modulates survival/apoptosis markers

changes: Removed TP53 from late_up: the cited desloratadine study reports TP53 mRNA upregulation, but TP53 is predominantly regulated post-translationally and is not a reliable transcriptional landmark for histamine receptor antagonism.
Removed NFKB2/RELB-type NF-kB subunits from consideration as proximal targets: no abstract supports direct NF-kB transcriptional suppression by histamine receptor antagonists.

Kept late_down proliferation genes (CCND1, CCNE2, CDK2/4/6, MYC, PCNA, MCM3, TOP2A, AURKA/B, BIRC5, CCNB1/2, CDK1) because the cited abstracts support growth inhibition and cell-cycle arrest, but flagged them as generic proliferation effects rather than direct histamine-receptor targets.

Kept late_up apoptosis/UPR/stress genes (CDKN1A, BAX, FAS, GADD45A, TRIB3, DDIT4, SQSTM1, BNIP3, BNIP3L, ATF5, CHAC1, XBP1, HERPUD1, DNAJB1, HSPA1A) because the cited abstracts support apoptosis, autophagy, and stress responses, but flagged them as generic downstream effects.

Retained line_response MCF7 as moderate based on PMID 41227370 (TP53-dependent apoptosis in MCF-7); other lines remain weak/none because no retrieved abstract provides line-specific transcriptional data.
Retained kinetics slow and magnitude weak/moderate because the cited abstracts report effects at 24-72 h and dose-dependent rather than immediate transcriptional responses.
Retained all five evidence citations because each abstract supports the stated claim about histamine receptor antagonism, apoptosis, autophagy, or histamine receptor expression.
